narrative: Material PL2__M79D742F exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=0.466) with a statistically significant upward trend over the 231-day history, and a right-skewed distribution indicating occasional demand spikes. Lead times are fast (mean 1.59 days) but moderately variable (CV=0.634), which drives the safety stock requirement. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 142,969 units consolidates replenishments from ~102 to ~9 orders per year, cutting total annual inventory costs by 80.5% while fully respecting the MOQ and storage capacity constraints.

research_insights.selection_rationale: High-volume near-continuous demand (96.5% non-zero days) with fast replenishment lead times makes a continuous-review (r,Q) policy appropriate. The large EOQ relative to the MOQ allows substantial order consolidation, and the low unit cost means holding a larger cycle stock is economically efficient versus frequent small orders.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap binds the EOQ: unconstrained quantity of 158,432 units was reduced to 142,969 to satisfy the 174,380-unit storage limit given a safety stock of 9,216. This leaves 22,195 units of headroom. If demand continues its upward trend, storage capacity may become a binding constraint within 6-12 months.
